note: The sender is a simulated interviewer. Clarification prompts are suggestions that the user must review, edit, and approve. Practice reduces uncertainty; it does not predict exact interview questions.
designNote: Clarifying a question is a professional communication strategy. The language is direct and respectful, without unnecessary apology or self-deprecation.

sampleMessages.text: Tell me about a time you balanced competing priorities while maintaining stakeholder alignment.
Tell me a little about yourself.
How do you usually handle pressure at work?

clarificationTypes.label: Which aspect should I focus on?
clarificationTypes.description: The question covers several areas. Ask which one matters most.

phrasings.text: Would you like me to focus on the technical decision or on how I worked with others?
To keep my answer focused, which part of the question matters most to you?
I can interpret this in a few ways. Which direction would be most useful for you?

clarificationTypes.label: Could we break this into parts?
clarificationTypes.description: The question has several parts. Ask to work through them one at a time.

phrasings.text: Could we break the question into smaller parts so I can answer each one clearly?
Which part would you like me to answer first?
To make sure I cover everything, may I take the question one part at a time?

clarificationTypes.label: Would you prefer an example or a general approach?
clarificationTypes.description: Clarify the expected level of detail before choosing an answer structure.

phrasings.text: Would you prefer a specific example from a project or a general explanation of my approach?
Should I go into one detailed example or keep the answer at a high level?
Would a specific example be most useful, or would you prefer a general approach?

clarificationTypes.label: Ask for a moment to organize your thoughts
clarificationTypes.description: Request a brief pause to organize the answer instead of rushing.

phrasings.text: Could I take a moment to organize my thoughts before I answer?
I would like to give you a complete answer. May I take a brief moment?
That is a useful question. May I think for a moment before answering?

responseExamples: Please focus on how you made the decision; I can ask about teamwork afterward.
Please use one specific example rather than a general answer.
Of course. Take a moment and answer when you are ready.
